thesis: Pulse has built credible upper-funnel momentum in the campaign period, with the strongest signal among younger consumers, but the tracker does not yet justify claiming equivalent behavioural conversion or campaign causality.

sections.headlineIntent: Frame the result as credible momentum with explicit limits, not a campaign victory lap.
sections.whyItMatters: The CMO needs to know whether competitive position moved and how confidently to talk about it.
caveats: Observed change is not causal proof.

sections.headlineIntent: Show the consideration improvement as the central competitive outcome, with younger consumers as an important explanatory cut where supported.
sections.whyItMatters: Consideration is closer to competitive intent than awareness alone.

sections.headlineIntent: Use campaign recognition and innovation imagery as supporting evidence that communications landed with the intended audience.
sections.whyItMatters: These measures help explain the pattern without being presented as proof of causation.
caveats: Supporting analysis results may be used even when not promoted to standalone gold findings in Turn 4.

sections.headlineIntent: Keep current usage/preference in view to show that upper-funnel momentum should not be confused with completed behavioural conversion.

excludedFindings.note: Important category context but not central to the Pulse campaign evaluation.
Strategically interesting but distracts from the campaign question.

tone: Confident but bounded; marketing-literate without attributing causality the design cannot establish.
